blocks.content: Quiz: What does const copy = [...original] create?
Tap an option below to answer:
A reference to the same array in memory
That would be const copy = original. Spread creates a new array, not a reference.
That would be const copy = original. Spread creates a new array, not a reference.
A shallow copy of the original array
Correct! Spread unpacks each element into a brand-new array. Changes to copy do not affect original.
Correct! Spread unpacks each element into a brand-new array. Changes to copy do not affect original.
A deep copy including all nested objects
Spread only copies one level deep. Nested objects are still shared by reference.
Spread only copies one level deep. Nested objects are still shared by reference.
Spread copies every element from the original. The result has the same elements, not zero.
Spread copies every element from the original. The result has the same elements, not zero.
